commentary.heading: Chipmakers weigh on Wall Street
commentary.body: US shares finished last week on a mixed note. On Friday the S&P 500 slipped 0.40% to 7,562 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.91% to 25,136, while the Dow managed a small gain. Semiconductor stocks led the selling, with AMD down almost 9% and Broadcom nearly 5%, as investors continued to digest Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia chief executive. Most sectors outside technology ended higher, and the S&P 500 still rose about 2.5% across the week.

commentary.heading: ASX gives back ground but holds a weekly gain
commentary.body: The ASX 200 fell 0.89% to 9,065.8 on Friday, with nine of the 11 sectors in the red. Property trusts and financials were the weakest areas as the major bank chiefs appeared before a parliamentary committee, and miners eased alongside lower copper, iron ore and gold prices. Even so, the index ended the week around 0.5% higher.

commentary.heading: Asian tech sold; London at a three-month high
commentary.body: Hong Kong's Hang Seng dropped 1.55% to 23,638, its third loss in a row, with Tencent off more than 3% on worries about the Nvidia leadership change and possible tighter US chip export rules. On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite eased 0.59% to 3,634 and the Shenzhen Component slid 2.05% to 10,969 as AI-linked shares were sold ahead of the Trump–Xi meeting. The FTSE 100 gained 0.40% to 10,906, supported by energy and healthcare, while the MSCI World index lost 0.38% to 4,852.

commentary.heading: Central banks and inflation
commentary.body: No central bank changed rates last week. US producer prices rose 0.3% in October, a little under expectations, after consumer prices climbed 0.4% for the month. Markets are pricing a December Fed rate rise as close to certain. The RBA cash rate stays at 4.85% after November's increase, and the Bank of England rate is 4.00%.

commentary.heading: Bonds, oil and the Australian dollar
commentary.body: Bond yields moved higher. The US 10-year yield ended near 5.15%, about 30 basis points up on the week, and the UK 10-year finished around 5.34%, while Australia's 10-year was little changed near 5.13%. Brent crude held around US$96 a barrel. A firmer US dollar left the Australian dollar at about 67.96 US cents, its weakest level since late January.

commentary.heading: What to watch
commentary.body: China's monthly activity figures are due on Monday and the US releases October retail sales on Tuesday. Nvidia reports quarterly results after the US close on Tuesday (Wednesday morning in Sydney), its first since the change of chief executive. Wednesday brings UK October inflation, minutes from the Fed's last meeting and the start of the Trump–Xi meeting. Australian October jobs data follow on Thursday and China's loan prime rate on Friday. Further out are Australia's October CPI and the Fed and RBA meetings on 9 and 8 December.
